newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes up on low dlr deamand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes up on low dlr deamand.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed higher against the dollar on Thursday due to lacklustre demand for the U.S. unit, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.80 to the dollar, after opening at 58.83 and then weakening to 58.87, they said.
"There was no commercial demand, but banks speculated on the dollar rising due to its overseas strength," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by 2.5 local cents, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.7021 and 59.8880.
"Speculators were beaten by high call money rates," said the Standard Chartered dealer.
Overnight call money closed at nine percent after rising to 12 percent, as it was squaring up day.
"But money should ease and bring banks back into dollars and push it (dollar) up to 59 rupees very soon," said a Hongkong Bank dealer.
